in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me review the information about your situation:

- You live in the UK
- You're asking about Alex, who is 15 years old and lives with you
- Alex is not in local authority care, hospital, or residential accommodation
- Alex doesn't work 24+ hours per week, hasn't started an apprenticeship, and doesn't receive qualifying benefits in their own right

Based on the UK Child Benefit rules, let me assess your eligibility:

**Key eligibility criteria:**
1. You normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK
2. You'll usually be responsible for a child if you live with them
3. Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child

In your case:
- ✓ You live in the UK
- ✓ Alex is 15 years old (under 16)
- ✓ Alex lives with you, which means you're responsible for them
- ✓ Alex doesn't fall into any of the disqualifying categories (not in care for 8+ weeks, not in hospital for 12+ weeks, not working 24+ hours/week, not receiving their own benefits)

Before I provide my final assessment, I need to confirm one important detail: **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (Remember, only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child.)

## **Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

**Summary:**
You meet all the standard eligibility requirements for Child Benefit:
- ✓ You live in the UK
- ✓ Alex is 15 years old (under 16)
- ✓ Alex lives with you (meaning you're responsible for them)
- ✓ No disqualifying factors apply

**Next steps:**
If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit for Alex, you should make a claim. Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, so ensure no one else is already claiming for Alex.

**Important note about the High Income Child Benefit Tax Charge:**
If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay a tax charge on the Child Benefit you receive. You can still claim Child Benefit but choose not to receive payments if you wish to avoid the charge, which helps protect your National Insurance record.

If you have any questions about how to claim or need more information, please feel free to ask!
